problem: Zero-shot VLM navigation methods (PIVOT, VLMnav) use fixed angular/distance action spaces and lack persistent spatial memory and soft constraints (e.g., warning signs), causing inefficient exploration and looping.
motivation: Fixed-interval action spaces are an idealized abstraction that leads to many small steps and high time cost, and geometric SLAM maps lack semantics usable by VLMs. Structured semantic memory queried by a VLM can help track visited places and reason about goals in long-horizon multi-goal tasks.
key_idea: Let a VLM pick free-form navigation targets from depth-derived ground candidate points, refined by the VLM for safety, and augment its decisions with a VLM-built self-updating graph memory of objects and spatial relations retrieved as text.
insight: Memory mainly improves path efficiency on ObjectNav (SPL 0.187 -> 0.232 with memory, SR 43.1 -> 45.0) and helps more on multi-subtask GOAT (SR 25.5 vs VLMnav 20.1). Restricting candidate sampling to the navigable ground plane is what separates VLMnav-style methods from PIVOT (22.7 SR). In the real-world example, memory lets the agent infer it is in a lab and leave to find the water dispenser, whereas the baseline loops near a faucet.
method: Memory Manager: VLM converts RGB-D observations into a graph G=(V,E) with object nodes (name, location, visual features/attributes) and spatial-relation edges, via add_node/add_edge functions.
Memory retrieval: spatial_query(semantic_filter) and path_inference(start,target) retrieve subgraphs that are converted to natural language for the VLM prompt; memory can be shared across robots.

Action Proposer (spatial sampling): navigable boundary from depth on the ground region in polar coordinates; uniform angular sampling with minimum angular gap θδ, far points preferred, distances scaled by α<1 for safety margin.
Action Proposer (safety filtering): VLM receives annotated image, candidate coordinates and natural-language constraints, removes unsafe points (near obstacles, signs) and adjusts positions/headings.
Action Selector: multimodal prompt [annotated image ⊕ task template ⊕ retrieved memory]; chain-of-thought gives confidence per candidate; argmax selects the action in polar coordinates (r,θ).
Stop check: separate VLM query on the original image gives s_stop; stop only if above threshold for 2 consecutive steps.

setting.backbone: Gemini 2.0 Flash-Lite (frozen, simulation); FastSAM for ground segmentation in the real world
setting.action_space: dynamic polar-coordinate target (r, θ) selected from VLM-refined candidate points on navigable ground

numbers.evidence: Table I ObjectNav Results: w/o Memory 43.1 / 0.187

numbers_note: Split names not stated in the paper (assumed 'val'); eval-set size not specified. Real-world results (SR out of 3-6 trials, ACD) are given in a table but are not benchmark numbers.
results: On HM3D ObjectNav DyNaVLM gets 45.0% SR / 0.232 SPL, beating VLMnav (42.8 / 0.218) and PIVOT (22.7 / 0.108). On GOAT-Bench it reaches 25.5% SR / 0.102 SPL, above VLMnav (20.1) and Modular GOAT SR (24.9), but below SenseAct-NN (29.5) and Modular GOAT's SPL (0.172). In real-world Go2 tests it outperforms VLMnav in SR on most tasks (e.g., water dispenser 3/6 vs 1/6).
limitations: Gap to specialized methods on GOAT (SR vs SenseAct-NN, SPL vs Modular GOAT); no explicit object localization
Small-scale real-world evaluation (3-6 trials per task) and only one memory ablation on ObjectNav; no GOAT ablation
Relies on a closed API VLM with likely high latency; cross-robot memory sharing claimed but not evaluated
